summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and PTSD was readmitted two days after discharge due to worsening bilateral lower extremity edema. She had developed pitting edema post-discharge, prompting a BNP check that revealed an elevated level of 703. She was admitted for a CHF workup. Evaluation included a normal echocardiogram with preserved ejection fraction (70%), moderate tricuspid regurgitation, and mild pulmonary hypertension, along with a normal chest X-ray and patent hepatic vasculature on Doppler ultrasound showing splenomegaly. Nephrotic syndrome and thrombosis were ruled out. She was managed with fluid and sodium restriction, diuresis using IV and oral furosemide, and close monitoring, resulting in a 4.8 kg weight loss. Her chronic right upper quadrant pain remained stable on home Dilaudid. She was discharged on oral furosemide, with instructions for daily weight monitoring and follow-up with primary care and gastroenterology.
